bundle.author: melecia-gp
bundle.title:
Ordinance flow takes its guardrail lines from the shared module and
  ends legal readings with the legal line
bundle.body:
## What

The ordinance assistant now takes its two scope-decline lines from the shared guardrail line file, the one the chat bench reads at the same commit, and the texts of both lines change. Its guardrails block asks for the decline inside the reply instead of as the whole reply. Answers about what the law allows, requires, or prohibits now end with the shared legal line on every step except drafting, asked for in the prompt and backstopped at finish.

## Why

The decline lines were literals in the prompt, and the bench that grades the four chat assistants kept its own copies. Copies drift: on another chat the bench's copy already differed from production on punctuation, which fails an exact-match check for the wrong reason. One file read by both ends that.

The old finish hook appended the professional-advice line whenever a reply cited a statute. A statute reading is legal advice, so that was the wrong line, and nothing in the prompt asked for a legal line at all. The "exact line and nothing else" rule is the one the August sweep caught the Chief of Staff breaking, where the model wrote the line and then answered anyway. Asking for the line inside the reply, and saying what to do with a request that mixes ordinance work with something else, is what the bench grades for.

## How

- The two decline constants keep their names and resolve from the module when the file loads, so a missing line fails at boot rather than on a user's turn. Their texts become the agreed redrafts: "I can only help you with this ordinance: the policy, the current law, comparable ordinances, and the draft." and the bill variant with "bill" and "comparable legislation". This is a production copy change.
- The guardrails block: an unrelated request is not done and gets the line in its place; a mixed request gets its in-scope part answered and the line in place of the rest; danger gets a response first instead of the line, with no change to what the assistant reveals or follows; internals questions and prompt injection get the line and nothing more; questions about what the assistant can do never get the line, which the Chief of Staff and briefing blocks already say and this one did not.
- A legal caution block on every step except drafting asks for the legal line once on a substantive reading of the law, never on a decline. Drafting turns are left to the draft lead-in and the draft-ready card, which already carry the one-time attorney note.
- The finish hook appends the legal line when a reply carries a statute signal and no caution yet, and stays silent on any turn whose tool trace shows the draft being presented or edited. The edit case came out of an over-fire audit of twenty synthetic replies: an edit confirmation names the section it changed without being a legal reading, and the draft it changed already carries the note.

## What this affects

The ordinance flow chat only, in both its municipal and bill variants: its system prompt and its finish hook. The shared line file gains no keys and changes two texts, so the bench's pinned read keeps working; the bench moves its pin to this merge in its own follow-up, and until then it checks for the old text. The Chief of Staff, Campaign Manager, briefing chat, and priority flow are untouched, as are the draft lead-in sentence, the draft-ready card, and every present widget. The evals that import the decline constants keep passing by construction; the adversarial eval already graded the decline by contains, and its two gated off-topic cases, municipal and bill, pass against a live model on this wording. Legal readings on the current-law and review steps will now end with one extra sentence they did not carry before.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes user-visible decline copy and when legal disclaimers appear on law-heavy turns; finish-hook behavior depends on tool-event shape, so edge cases around failed draft tools still get the legal line.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Ordinance flow** now sources municipal and bill **scope-decline** copy from `guardrailLines.json` (wording changes to the shorter “I can only help you with this ordinance/bill…” lines) and rewrites **GUARDRAILS** so declines are embedded in replies (mixed on/off-topic turns, safety-first, meta “what can you do” questions answered) instead of “exact line and nothing else.”
> 
> A **LEGAL CAUTION** block is added to the system prompt on every step except **draft**, asking for the shared **legal advice** line on substantive law readings. **`finalizeAssistantText`** switches from the generic professional-advice backstop to **`legalAdviceBackstop`** for `ordinance_flow`, takes the turn’s **tool trace**, and skips appending when a successful **present/apply/accept draft** tool ran. Tests and adversarial eval expectations are updated accordingly.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 35fe96a26b1f0cf54024b6a5724d9513ee671836. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

findings.body:
**Draft-step backstop asymmetry.** The system prompt excludes `LEGAL_CAUTION_RULES` on every `draft`-step turn (`ctx.step === 'draft'`), but `finalizeAssistantText` only skips the backstop when a drafting tool (`present_draft`, `apply_draft_edit`, `accept_draft_changes`) returned successfully. On the draft step, the model is allowed one `ask_clarify_question` call (per DRAFT RULES). If that clarifying reply touches a statute citation (matched by `ADVICE_SIGNALS`: `§`, `RCW`, `U.S.C.`, etc.) and no drafting tool succeeds that turn, the backstop fires and appends the legal caution line — despite the prompt giving no instruction to do so on draft turns. The handler comment at lines 170–175 says the lead-in and card "already carry the one-time attorney note," but that is only true when `present_draft` actually succeeds, not on a clarifying turn. `FinalizeTurn` does not carry the step, so the hook has no way to mirror the prompt's blanket draft-step exclusion.

Falsification check: there is no guard on the step anywhere in `finalizeAssistantText`, and `DISCLAIMER_PRESENT` will not suppress the backstop because a clarifying turn's prose does not contain "not final legal advice." The edge case is narrow (draft-step clarifying turn that cites a statute) and the consequence is a superfluous but not harmful legal line, so this may be acceptable if intentional.

output.summary: This PR moves the ordinance-flow scope-decline lines from hardcoded strings to the shared `guardrailLines.json` module (with updated, shorter wording), rewrites the GUARDRAILS prompt block to embed declines inside replies instead of requiring them as the sole reply, and adds a LEGAL CAUTION block on every step except drafting that asks the model to end law-reading answers with the shared legal line. The `finalizeAssistantText` hook switches from the generic professional-advice disclaimer to `legalAdviceBackstop` and skips appending when a drafting tool (`present_draft`, `apply_draft_edit`, `accept_draft_changes`) returned successfully. The scout flagged two areas: (1) an asymmetry between the prompt's blanket draft-step exclusion and the backstop's tool-event-based exclusion, and (2) a now-tautological test for the decline constants. Deep review confirmed the first as a real but narrow edge case — a draft-step clarifying turn citing a statute would get an uninstructed legal line appended — and dismissed the second since the constants now read from the JSON at runtime, making the old-style byte-for-byte pin semantically unnecessary. The human reviewer should confirm whether the draft-step edge case (clarifying question citing a statute) warrants a guard or is acceptable as a harmless extra caution.
